reviewStatus: Fresh revision-2 author evidence mapping. No earlier PASS status carries forward. Author checks do not replace independent parent review. Linked source pages and current service availability were not independently verified.

source.title: AI in Financial Services: Research Summary & CDW Seller Playbook
source.location: Local supplied Markdown file. Not copied into this draft or a served directory.
source.evidenceRule: All section citations refer to the supplied compilation, not independent retrieval of its linked source documents. Dates on offering claims identify the compilation date, not a verified publication date for a live offering page.

authoringPolicy.fiction: All customers, companies, figures, dialogue, scenarios, quiz situations, and outcomes are fictional training examples. The selected Microsoft 365 Copilot and Five9 products are fictional customer choices, not testimonials or entitlement claims.
authoringPolicy.measurement: Customer measures are fictional inputs or authored evaluation proposals. They are not audited results, promised returns, or service commitments.
authoringPolicy.misconceptions: Nonideal choices contain premature or false claims only with immediate corrective coaching. They are not recommended product claims.
authoringPolicy.proposedControls: Working meetings, consent rules, non-recording alternatives, approved samples, test measures, and escalation paths are authored recommendations. They are not extra named-service deliverables.
authoringPolicy.availability: Confirm current scope and availability. FinOps for AI, AI Value Assurance, Agents & Workflow Automation, Hyperscaler AI Foundation, AI-Accelerated Engineering, and Modern Data Ecosystem Design Workshop are Coming Soon. Security from AI is under construction. None appears in this curriculum.
authoringPolicy.distribution: Keep evidence outside the web root. Local authoring does not authorize publication. Audience and hosting approval remain separate.

claims.claim: The named customer, work practices, dialogue, and possible outcomes are invented training examples.
claims.caveat: Sector context is informed by the compilation. No customer testimony, measured result, or promised commitment is claimed.

claims.claim: Discover document authority and updates before testing internal procedure search. Compare correct answers, checking time, access, and escalation.
claims.caveat: The branch procedure story, source-link proposal, sample meeting, and test design are authored recommendations. No search accuracy or ready-made integration is promised.

claims.claim: AI Readiness Data Quality Assessment is a source-described response to fragmented or untrusted data and document-search needs.
claims.caveat: Positioned only if structured investigation is needed. Confirm current scope and availability. No named deliverables beyond the supplied scope are claimed.

claims.claim: Private hosting does not by itself establish security or approval.
claims.caveat: The nonideal seller reply deliberately overstates hosting. Its immediate coaching rejects that inference. Bank approval remains a separate decision.

claims.claim: The named customer, work practices, dialogue, and possible outcomes are invented training examples.
claims.caveat: Sector context is informed by the compilation. No customer testimony, measured result, or promised commitment is claimed.

claims.claim: Investigate the coordinator-to-adjuster handoff and test document completeness before assignment. Measure checking, corrections, and waiting separately.
claims.caveat: Claims extraction and intake are source-supported directions, often not mature deployments. This exact checklist, handoff, test, and working session are authored proposals, not a packaged service.

claims.claim: The source does not establish a ready-made autonomous settlement service for this customer or authority to substitute invented facts.
claims.caveat: High-stakes claims require human review in the source. Nonideal replies propose settlement or substituting estimated facts and receive immediate corrective coaching.

claims.claim: The named customer, work practices, dialogue, and possible outcomes are invented training examples.
claims.caveat: Sector context is informed by the compilation. No customer testimony, measured result, or promised commitment is claimed.

claims.claim: Explore advisor-reviewed notes and follow-up, client consent, a non-recording route, corrections, and total work rather than login counts.
claims.caveat: The Morgan Stanley example supports this general direction, not a Microsoft feature claim or CDW turnkey integration. Consent rules, the alternative route, and trial measures are authored proposals.

claims.claim: Copilot Adoption and Change Management appears under AI Assistants for customers on a chosen platform with adoption needs.
claims.caveat: The fictional firm chose Microsoft 365 Copilot. Current scope and availability require confirmation. No notes integration, recording entitlement, or guaranteed savings are asserted.

claims.claim: The compilation does not establish fully autonomous advice or approval-free client follow-up.
claims.caveat: This is an evidence limit, not a claim about all possible market capabilities. The nonideal reply receives immediate correction.

claims.claim: The named customer, work practices, dialogue, and possible outcomes are invented training examples.
claims.caveat: Sector context is informed by the compilation. No customer testimony, measured result, or promised commitment is claimed.

claims.claim: FirstTouch AI covers the first minute of contact on supported platforms, including Five9. Platform support alone does not establish a particular transfer integration.
claims.caveat: The source describes scope as of compilation, not verified current availability. Trace this fictional handoff before recommending a service. No dispute decision or refund authority follows.

claims.claim: Trace what callers provide and staff receive, then compare repeated questions, missing details, and staff checking time.
claims.caveat: The payment-dispute handoff and evaluation are authored hypotheses. Payments-specific generative evidence is thin and does not prove a ready-made dispute integration.

claims.claim: The source does not demonstrate that FirstTouch AI decides or issues refunds. Consequential actions need separately bounded authority.
claims.caveat: The compilation describes agent-initiated payments as emerging. This lesson separates first contact from refund authority without asserting that ordinary payment automation is new.

claims.claim: Copying is repetitive work, not confirmed rework. Ask about time and corrections.
claims.caveat: Rework is not established by the fictional question.

claims.claim: Follow the staff procedure search to learn where it slows down.
claims.caveat: The question does not diagnose the cause of the search delay.

claims.claim: Investigate the full note workflow before prescribing training for continued evening work.
claims.caveat: The chosen product and evening work are fictional. Access, habits, and correction effort remain possibilities, not established causes.

claims.claim: A board request establishes pressure, not a confirmed sponsor or resources.
claims.caveat: Sponsorship and resources require discovery. They cannot be inferred from the fictional request.

claims.claim: Investigate the transfer problem before accepting a proposed phone-menu solution.
claims.caveat: This is an authored discovery recommendation. No integration or cause is established.

claims.claim: Explore a source-checked claim summary while leaving the claim decision with adjusters.
claims.caveat: Task fit does not promise accuracy or autonomous settlement.

claims.claim: Separate finding approved instructions from authority to change customer records.
claims.caveat: The proposed search is an authored bounded task, not an existing implementation.

claims.claim: Keep notes and follow-up as drafts for advisor review under consent rules.
claims.caveat: This is an authored task boundary informed by the disclosed wealth workflow, not a CDW product capability claim.

claims.claim: Explore identifying missing estimates earlier rather than accelerating already-quick summaries.
claims.caveat: The proposed completeness check is a hypothesis, not proof it reduces the wait.

claims.claim: Start with the known missing dispute reason rather than unsettled refund authority.
claims.caveat: Payments document-work evidence is thin. The handoff proposal is not proof of deployment or guaranteed fit.

claims.claim: Ask where loss dates come from and inspect document formats before testing extraction.
claims.caveat: No input quality or standard format is assumed.

claims.claim: Establish the approved document and its owner before search uses conflicting procedures.
claims.caveat: File dates alone do not establish authority. This is an authored discovery recommendation.

claims.claim: Trace an approved example from capture to employee screen before diagnosing a missing handoff.
claims.caveat: The recorded reason and missing screen information are fictional. The cause remains unknown.

claims.claim: Define which work a time measure includes before comparing a new check.
claims.caveat: The 10-minute figure is fictional. Total work and waiting must not be silently excluded.

claims.claim: FirstTouch AI covers the first minute of customer contact on supported platforms. Qualification requires a platform decision and current service-fit checks.
claims.caveat: The source excludes customers without a platform decision. A supported platform does not guarantee a particular task or integration.

claims.claim: Treat an unsupported date in a generated summary as an error requiring source checking.
claims.caveat: The date error is fictional. Review and escalation are authored controls, not guarantees.

claims.claim: Resolve client consent before recording. Tool access and advisor approval are distinct.
claims.caveat: The client-consent boundary is informed by the disclosed wealth workflow. The firm must decide its own applicable rules.

claims.claim: Test access restrictions before expanding internal search.
claims.caveat: The access failure is fictional. Internal use does not authorize all staff to read all records.

claims.claim: AI Risk Assessment informs risk decisions and does not grant approval.
claims.caveat: Current scope requires confirmation. The assessment does not replace bank approval or guarantee compliance or security.

claims.claim: A successful information-transfer test does not establish refund authority.
claims.caveat: The successful test is fictional and deliberately narrow. No autonomous refund capability is asserted.

claims.claim: Agree approved examples and data protection before accepting customer files.
claims.caveat: The proposed control is authored, not a named service deliverable or universal legal rule.

claims.claim: Bring coordinator and adjuster leads together around returned and completed files.
claims.caveat: This is an authored working meeting, not a source-prescribed engagement.

claims.claim: Copilot Adoption and Change Management is a source-described option for support on a chosen platform.
claims.caveat: The service appears in coaching, not the required answer. Confirm current scope and inspect correction effort before promising a solution.

claims.claim: Explore work-specific training and support for reviewing meeting notes when generic training omitted that work.
claims.caveat: The chosen platform, access, and training gap are fictional. The proposed support follows those premises without requiring service-name recall.

claims.claim: Offer a decision plan for document and risk review without committing to launch by a board date.
claims.caveat: The 6-week deadline and proposed review are fictional training details, not service commitments.

claims.claim: Private AI Launch Workshop may fit strategy and privacy exploration.
claims.caveat: The service appears in coaching. Confirm current workshop scope, and do not imply deployment or a required hosting choice.

claims.claim: Agree a useful task, information needs, and decision owners in a first working session.
claims.caveat: The competing ideas and privacy concerns are fictional. The working session is an authored recommendation, not a named-service deliverable.

claims.claim: Measure current copying and checking time, errors, and corrections before a test.
claims.caveat: These are proposed measures for the fictional task, not proof of savings.

claims.claim: Include checking in total work. A 3-minute draft and 12-minute check exceed a previous 10-minute task.
claims.caveat: All numbers are fictional. This arithmetic illustrates net time, not customer results.

claims.claim: Shorter calls alone do not demonstrate less repeated explanation at transfer.
claims.caveat: The reported change is fictional and does not prove better handoff information.

claims.claim: Test representative document types and agree how people handle failures before rollout.
claims.caveat: The sample design is authored. Good results on clear files do not establish results on handwritten files.

claims.claim: Separate faster intake from unchanged total claim resolution and investigate the remaining wait.
claims.caveat: The local improvement is fictional. It is not audited return evidence or a service guarantee.

claims.claim: Explore a completeness check before assignment, involve both handoff owners, and compare local effort with overall resolution.
claims.caveat: The scenario states actual file returns for missing estimates. The proposed task and measures are hypotheses to test, not permission to settle claims or a packaged service.
